en.title: James Gunn Drops 12 Essential Body Horror Flicks Before Clayface Arrives
en.summary: Ahead of DC's R-rated dive into monstrous transformation with Clayface, filmmaker James Gunn shared his must-watch body horror list. Fans are already dissecting the curated collection of visceral cinema.
en.body:
The maestro behind Guardians of the Galaxy and The Suicide Squad, **James Gunn**, has offered a potent prescription for anyone bracing themselves for DC's upcoming R-rated exploration of monstrous transformation: a list of 12 body horror films that hold a special place in his cinematic heart. With **Clayface** slated for release on October 23, 2026, Gunn took to Threads to share his curated watchlist, designed to immerse audiences in the genre's unsettling depths before they face the shape-shifting villain.

This isn't just any collection of creepy movies; it's a masterclass in visceral storytelling. Gunn's picks read like a who's who of body horror's most influential architects. Unsurprisingly, the list is heavily populated by the unsettling visions of **David Cronenberg**, the undisputed titan of the subgenre. Titles like **Shivers**, **The Brood**, **Videodrome**, and **The Fly** showcase his unparalleled ability to twist the human form into something both terrifying and profoundly disturbing. Complementing Cronenberg's work are genre-defining classics such as **John Carpenter's The Thing**, a masterclass in paranoia and practical effects, and **Philip Kaufman's 1978 Invasion of the Body Snatchers**, which taps into primal fears of assimilation. Other notable inclusions like **Stuart Gordon's Re-Animator** and **Frank Henenlotter's Basket Case** bring a more darkly comedic, often outrageous, edge to the proceedings, proving that body horror can be as much about gonzo fun as it is about existential dread.

## A Deep Dive into Disturbing Delights

The selection is remarkably cohesive, leaning into films that explore the violation and mutation of the physical self. **Altered States**, directed by **Ken Russell**, offers a mind-bending journey into consciousness and physical degradation, while **Chuck Russell's The Blob** (the 1988 remake, presumably, though not explicitly stated) provides a more contemporary, effects-driven take on parasitic horror. **James Gunn** even included his own 2006 film, **Slither**, a gleefully grotesque alien invasion story that cemented his own distinctive voice within the genre. It's a list that respects the history of body horror, from its more philosophical explorations to its most gleefully gruesome manifestations, all while building anticipation for what **Clayface** might bring to the DC Universe.

## Preparing for DC's Next Monstrous Tale

For fans of **Clayface**, this list is more than just a recommendation; it's a roadmap. It signifies the film's commitment to exploring the psychological and physical horror inherent in the villain's origin. The sheer variety within Gunn's picks—spanning decades and directorial styles—suggests that **Clayface** will likely embrace the genre's full spectrum. The anticipation for this R-rated take on a classic Batman foe is palpable, and Gunn's thoughtful curation only amplifies the excitement. It’s a clear signal that DC is ready to push boundaries and deliver a horror experience that is both artistically significant and viscerally impactful.

## What's Next

With **Clayface** set to unleash its particular brand of horror on October 23, 2026, fans have ample time to explore Gunn's recommended viewing. Whether you're a seasoned body horror aficionado or a curious newcomer, this list promises a journey through some of the most unsettling and unforgettable films ever made.

It’s the season to yell at your friends about which horror movies they should watch (HAVE YOU HEARD THE GOOD WORD ABOUT LET’S SCARE JESSICA TO DEATH?!?!? ), and James Gunn has gotten in on the fun by sharing his list of body horror films that are “close to his heart” and will help you get in the mood for DC’s upcoming body horror film, Clayface . For reference, here is the list of movies that Gunn shared via Threads : Altered States , directed by Ken Russell Basket Case , directed by Frank Henenlotter Cronos , directed by Guillermo del Toro Invasion of the Body Snatchers , directed by Philip Kaufman (1978) Re-Animator , directed by Stuart Gordon Shivers , directed by David Cronenberg Slither , directed by James Gunn The Blob , directed by Chuck Russell The Brood , directed by David Cronenberg The Fly , directed by David Cronenberg The Thing , directed by John Carpenter Videodrome , directed by David Cronenberg To be honest, there’s not a bad movie in the bunch. Unsurprisingly, Gunn recommends nearly all of the body horror works of director David Cronenberg: the most influential figure in the history of the film subgenre. If you’ve never dived deep into the works of Cronenberg… well, there might be better places to start if you consider yourself particularly averse to the entire body horror concept. The Fly is arguably the body horror movie, but its popularity is a testament to its quality rather than its status as a relatively tame entry point. The unlisted Dead Ringers (which is really more of a spiritual and thematic body horror film) may be your better Cronenberg starting point before you work your way into Videodrome , The Fly , and eventually, Shivers and The Brood . Cronos , Altered States , and The Thing are slightly more friendly entry points for newcomers. Cronos in particular is a fantastic way to familiarize yourself with the concepts of the body horror genre within the confines of an exceptional vampire story. Invasion of the Body Snatchers may be the biggest “must-watch” of the bunch, though, due to both its status as arguably one of the greatest horror films ever made and its thematic relevance to the Vince Gilligan series, Pluribus . It’s also funny that Gunn included Chuck Russell’s Blob remake alongside his own Slither . Both are very good, but the former was quite certainly an influence on the latter.
